Gniewoszów Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Gniewoszów, Poland

Demolished. The Jewish community of Gniewoszów likely formed around the same time as its synagogue, first recorded in 1748, though the cemetery itself isn't confirmed until burial-fee records from 1844. By 1921, 585 Jews made up two-thirds of the town's population; most were deported to Treblinka in 1942. Wartime looting stripped the cemetery of its tombstones and wall, and Poland formally closed it in 1964. The site also holds an unmarked chapter of postwar violence: five of Gniewoszów's last Holocaust survivors were killed in 1945, and are presumed buried here. Descendants and the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage restored a partial fence in 2014, recovering and mounting dozens of tombstones on its walls, and added a memorial plaque to the 1945 victims in 2019.
